scope: Only R18 56 originally visible complete tests, original repository bytes and frozen R27 declaration inventory. No R31 selection or any generated test, evaluation label or native outcome.

policy.assertions: Python assert; source-imported Go testify require/assert call arguments excluding testing context; source-imported TypeScript expect input and outer matcher arguments.
policy.trace: Direct call names and receiver/argument values; recurse through a unique simple earlier local assignment. TypeScript requires const. No copies from bare-name aliases, tuple/destructure writes, rebindings, conditional assignments, callbacks or helper-body expansion. Unknowns remain explicit.
policy.order: Original inherited anchor order, original assertion byte order, then source call byte order; source declarations by path/start/id. No issue/API/task ranking.
policy.retrieval: Exact terminal callee-name match against frozen full inventory. All alternatives retained as ambiguity. Complete declaration docs/header plus the inventory's one-layer owner-doc group; no implementation bodies.
policy.budget: One deduplicated catalog shared across all anchors/assertions of each trial. Each complete declaration+owner group is admitted in the fixed order only if the catalog stays <=24000 bytes; skipped groups remain in ledger. Also project replacing only R18 issue_api_catalog while retaining the entire rest of the generation prompt under 96000 bytes.
policy.limits: This is contract-context retrieval, not oracle truth, API binding, reachability proof, test generation or a new detector. Scalar fields/properties without calls are outside this rule. Existing source assumptions may be wrong.

rows.scope_limit: Original Go anchors use table loops and testing.T failure branches, outside the bound testify assertion adapter. Zero recognized roots is unsupported extraction, not no original assertions.
Original Go anchors use if predicates followed by testing.T.Error/Fatal calls. This conditional-assertion form is outside the narrow adapter and was not rewritten as a semantic assertion.
Original TypeScript anchors rely on a global expect with no source import binding. The census abstains from treating a same-named global as a bound assertion framework.
The require import is the repository-owned github.com/d5/tengo/v2/require package, not the recognized testify package. Its assertion-helper semantics are not inferred from the name.
Same repository-owned require package as P5. No helper-body expansion or new assertion adapter was added.

conclusion: All matched call-derived declaration IDs already belong to the R27 candidate union. The rule changes context priority and which complete documentation can be shown; it does not introduce a new declaration universe.
Name-only matches remain highly ambiguous. N07 needs 48,950 bytes before budgeting and omits 26 groups; N08 needs 262,963 bytes and omits 200 groups under the shared 24KB cap.
Five trials have no supported assertion roots under this conservative adapter set. Their empty catalogs do not show an absence of useful oracle contracts.
The included catalogs fit the inherited complete 96KB generation envelopes, but fit does not establish usefulness, binding or correctness.

The N08 omitted original TestWaitForDurability anchor is outside the fixed 56 inputs; this census cannot inspect its SeqNum bound through a missing anchor. Scalar fields such as event metadata are not method call names and are also outside this rule.
decision: Preserve this finite source census. Do not implement a selector or broaden dataflow/assertion adapters in this round. New omitted-anchor recovery must remain a separate experiment.
